page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Running head at the top, with the page number at the top left. No marginal notes. The catchword is at the bottom right.

main_text.p: perio, præstantissimo Theologo, nobiscum aliàs de Authore sentienti, excidisse miramur. Sic enim vocibus sua authoritas, suum pondus, sua quædam perit ἐνέργεια[?]. Sic nullibi Pauli oratio est, sed quorundam forte amanuensium. Quum ne quidem ipse ille Tertus, Rom. xvi. 22, tam scripserit Epistolam, quàm juxtà Syrum Interpretem, descripserit. iv. Si Paulus dictavit, dubio procul etiam verba. Non enim res dictaverit sine verbis. Hæc ergò accuratissimè notarius exceperit, & credibilius Pauli expressisse voces, quàm novas de suo finxisse. v. Absurdum, & propè ad impietatem accedit quod habet Bellarminus, scribam hujusce Epistolæ, magis disertum fuisse, quàm ipse qui scribà Paulus utebatur. Cedo nobis illum amanuensem, tanto Apostolo, & inter omnes Scriptores Sacros, eloquentiæ laude conspicuo, disertiorem? vi. Vel γραμματεύς Scriba ille fuit, vel inferioris ordinis & authoritatis. Si posterius, quantum Epistolæ detrahitur? Quàm eloquij illa majestas deprimitur, infrà illa omnia

page.notes: The first word "perio" is in italic and its first letters are doubtful; it may be the end of a longer word from the previous page, so the fragment is kept as printed. The Greek word after "perit" is only partly legible; the reading ἐνέργεια is a guess from the visible ending. The Greek word after "vi. Vel" is also only partly legible; γραμματεύς is a guess from its shape. The Greek word at the end of "Vel" line is printed with a small mark before it, which is not transcribed. The catchword "quæ" is printed at the right below the last line.
